## What it is

ArchiveBox saves web pages you choose so they stay readable after the site changes or disappears, or when the box is offline. For each link it keeps several copies: HTML, a PDF, a screenshot, the text, and media where it can ([ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox)). It is the Supply Depot's archiving app (issue #129, NMD-04).

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L1**. The research licence matrix has a v0.9.77 row, so the licence gate can confirm it.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment`, one container: `docker.io/archivebox/archivebox:0.9.77`, pinned by digest (Docker Hub registry API, 2026-11-19; amd64 and arm64). The image bundles Chromium and the other archivers, so it is large (about 1 GB compressed per architecture).
- **Why it can run non-root:** the image sets no `USER`, but its entrypoint (`bin/docker_entrypoint.sh` at v0.9.77) has an explicit non-root path: when it is not root it skips every `chown`, only checks that the folders it needs are writable, and runs as the current user. The image's `Dockerfile` already gives those folders (`/opt/archivebox`, the home folder, `/tmp/archivebox`) to UID/GID 911. So the pod runs as 911, and `fsGroup: 911` makes the data volume writable.
- **Data:** the whole collection (database, config, every snapshot) lives on the PVC `archivebox-data` (20Gi) at `/data`.
- **Private by default:** `PUBLIC_INDEX=False` and `PUBLIC_ADD_VIEW=False`, so visitors without an account can neither browse the archive nor add links (upstream's default for the index is public).
- The root filesystem stays writable (the entrypoint writes under `/opt/archivebox`, the home folder and `/tmp`). RuntimeDefault seccomp, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped, no service-account token.
- **Chromium sandbox:** the image sets `CHROME_SANDBOX=false`, so Chromium's own sandbox is off and the container (non-root, no capabilities, own namespace) is the boundary around pages it loads. Only archive sites you trust that far.
- Probes: `GET /health/` with the Host header `admin.archivebox.localhost:5797`, as in upstream's own health check (the server routes by host name). The startup probe allows 10 minutes for the first `archivebox init`.
- Requests 100m CPU / 512Mi, limit 2 CPU / 2Gi: OneMind choices; Chromium snapshots need the headroom.

## First run

Source: [ArchiveBox wiki, Docker](https://github.com/ArchiveBox/ArchiveBox/wiki/Docker).

1. Install ArchiveBox from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-archivebox`; the first start creates the collection.
2. Create the admin account (you type the password; nothing is stored in the manifests):
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-archivebox exec -it deploy/archivebox -- archivebox manage createsuperuser
   ```
3. Forward the port and open http://localhost:5797, log in, and add a URL.
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-archivebox port-forward svc/archivebox 5797:5797
   ```

## Not done yet

- Archiving needs the internet (it fetches the pages); reading the saved copies does not.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the app is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; they are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.
